How the hardware connects

A few words.
A way forward.

The small thing captures your thought. Your OpenAGI brings the memory, context, and tools. The connection between them depends on the hardware.

01

Capture.

Press the device’s button and record a thought. Its recording indicator makes capture visible. The exact controls depend on the device.

02

Connect.

Move the audio or synced context through a phone app, a documented integration, or a bridge you build. Bluetooth alone does not provide access to recordings.

03

Make it useful.

On your computer or server, OpenAGI can use the context with your tools—for notes, questions, and tasks. The available reply path depends on the adapter.

✳

Your agent has a home.

The full OpenAGI runtime lives on your computer or server. Rings keep their own firmware and connect through an app; a development board can run a custom device client.

Set up OpenAGI ↗

One idea. Four different connections.

Follow the path
for your device.

These are proposed connection routes. None of the four has a tested OpenAGI adapter yet.

Sample inquiry · SDK unconfirmed

eIoT RC01

Ring → phone companion → OpenAGI

Needs the supplier SDK, a sample, and an OpenAGI adapter.

Read the guide ↗
Retail listing · MCP route documented

Vocci Ring

Ring → Vocci app → MCP → OpenAGI

OpenAGI integration is proposed; live voice streaming is unverified.

Read the guide ↗
Waitlist · OpenAGI access unconfirmed

Natura Interface

Ring → NatureOS → access to be confirmed

No verified OpenAGI SDK or connection yet.

Read the guide ↗
Development hardware · Firmware required

Waveshare AMOLED

Device → Wi-Fi bridge → OpenAGI

Vendor examples exist; custom firmware and host bridge remain.
